:::{#lem-cross-term-zero}
#### The conditional mean's error is uncorrelated with any function of the input

Let $g^*(\Predvar) \eqdef \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}$.
For any prediction function $g(\Predvar)$ with $\E{g(\Predvar)^2} < \infty$:

$$\E{\prederr_{g^*} \cd \paren{g(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)}} = 0$$

:::

::: proof

Because $g(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)$ is a function of $\Predvar$,
by @thm-cond-pull-out it factors out of the conditional expectation:

$$
\ba
\E{\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)} \mid \Predvar}
&= \paren{g(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)} \cd \E{\prederr_{g^*} \mid \Predvar}
&& \text{(a function of } \Predvar \text{ factors out)} \\
&= \paren{g(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)} \cd \E{g^*(\Predvar) - \Outvar \mid \Predvar}
&& \text{(definition of } \prederr_{g^*} \text{)} \\
&= \paren{g(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)} \cd \paren{\E{g^*(\Predvar) \mid \Predvar} - \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}
&& \text{(linearity of conditional expectation)} \\
&= \paren{g(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)} \cd \paren{g^*(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)}
&& \text{(a function of } \Predvar \text{ is its own conditional mean, and definition of } g^*(\Predvar) \text{)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(evaluate)}
\ea
$$

By the law of iterated expectations (@thm-lie):

$$
\ba
\E{\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)}}
&= \E{\E{\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g(\Predvar) - g^*(\Predvar)} \mid \Predvar}}
&& \text{(law of iterated expectations)} \\
&= \E{0}
&& \text{(the conditional expectation is } 0 \text{)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(expectation of a constant)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-cross-term-zero}
#### The vanishing cross term in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor, take $g_1(\Predvar) = 3$.
When $\Predvar = 0$, $g^*(0) = 1$, so $g_1(0) - g^*(0) = 2$,
and $\prederr_{g^*} = 1 - \Outvar$ is $1$ or $-1$ with equal probability,
so the product has conditional mean $0$.
The same cancellation happens when $\Predvar = 1$,
so the expectation of the product is $0$.

:::
